$comment: `tct_token` is a literal committed ES256 JWS, not a placeholder, and a minter MUST NOT re-sign it. It was signed by kat-keypair-005-p256 over `tct_token_claims` (RFC 6979 deterministic k, low-S), and then S was replaced by n - S, where n is the P-256 group order. The low-S twin (the same token with S restored) verifies under the issuer key; scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs derives it and asserts that it verifies, that the committed high-S token passes a lax ECDSA check, and that the §5.4.7 strict check rejects it.
description: TCT compact JWS signed ES256 by a P-256 issuer whose signature has a high S value (S > n/2). The header, claims and the ECDSA equation are all valid: a stock JOSE ES256 verifier accepts the token. RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.7 requires verifiers to reject S > n/2, for compact JWS as for the JCS profile, so receivers MUST reject with TCT_SIGNATURE_INVALID (RFC-AITP-0005 §7.2 step 4).

expected.rationale: Header is {"alg":"ES256","typ":"aitp-tct+jwt"}, which matches the P-256 `iss` AID, so the `typ` and `alg` checks (steps 2-3) pass. The signature satisfies the ECDSA equation but carries S > n/2, which RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.7 forbids, so step 4 rejects it. A verifier that accepts this token is wrapping an off-the-shelf JOSE library without the §5.4.7 low-S check.
